instructions: Peel the tinda, trim off the tops, and cut a shallow cross into the top of each one.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the tinda, cover, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until partly cooked. Transfer them to a plate.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion. Mince the garlic and grate the ginger together. Slit the green chili. Grate the tomatoes on the large holes of a box grater and throw away the skins.
In a large pot, heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until soft. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the coriander powder, chili powder and turmeric, and cook for 20 seconds. Add the grated tomato, the green chili and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the oil shows at the edges of the masala.
Add 1 cup of water, cover, and simmer on medium-low for 5 minutes.
Add the tinda and coat them in the gravy. Cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until a knife slides into a tinda easily.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the cilantro. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Ruchi's Kitchen (the lead) part-cooks the tinda, builds an onion, ginger, garlic and tomato masala with cumin, coriander and turmeric, then simmers the tinda in the gravy. Nisha Madhulika and My Weekend Kitchen use a faster tomato-only masala with fennel and no onion. This version follows the lead, scaled for 4, and grates the tomatoes in place of the home-made puree. The tinda cook in a separate pan while the masala goes, which is how it fits in about 45 minutes. Ghee is swapped for oil to keep it vegan.
